title: When Single-Agent with Skills Replace Multi-Agent Systems and When They Fail
relevance_note: Direct single-agent versus multi-agent topology comparison with scaling failure analysis.
reason_included: Provides explicit tradeoff between external coordination and internal skill selection, plus failure threshold.

claim_snippets.claim_text: In the compiled setting, token consumption drops by 53.7% on average because the single agent avoids repeated cross-agent context re-encoding while maintaining competitive accuracy.

Skill selection remains stable only up to a capacity threshold; once large skill libraries are reached, accuracy drops sharply, but hierarchical routing recovers about 37-40 points for GPT-4o-mini when |S| is at least 60.
The paper compiles sequential multi-agent workflows into a single agent that internally invokes structured skills such as decompose, solve, and verify within one shared context window.
